---
title: "Set up your workspace"
---

## Open the project

Have R, Quarto and VS Code or RStudio installed. Use an R/Bioconductor combination that supplies **ANCOMBC 2.16.0 or newer** for the expanded inference stage. You may need to update R if your compatible Bioconductor release supplies an older ANCOMBC.
[Download the project](https://github.com/tmbuza/ai-assisted-microbiome-analysis),
extract it and open its main folder. Apply this update there before using the
new commands. Open a terminal in the folder containing `_quarto.yml`.

You should see `data/`, `scripts/R/`, `config/`, `examples/` and `templates/`.
Run all analysis commands from this folder.

## Restore and extend the R environment

Start R in the terminal:

```bash
R
```

At the R prompt, restore the existing project lockfile if present, then add the
packages needed for this expanded workflow:

```r
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
if (!requireNamespace("renv", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("renv")
if (file.exists("renv.lock")) renv::restore()
renv::install(c("ggplot2", "vegan"))
renv::install("bioc::ANCOMBC")
renv::snapshot()
renv::status()
```

Follow installation prompts and resolve errors before continuing. ANCOMBC
adds Bioconductor dependencies; installation can take longer than exploration
packages. Use a Bioconductor release compatible with your R version. Do not
force a development version or replace packages at random to bypass an error.

```r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(vegan))
packageVersion("ANCOMBC")
stopifnot(packageVersion("ANCOMBC") >= numeric_version("2.16.0"))
q(save = "no")
```

Commands beginning `Rscript` or `quarto` run in the terminal. R expressions
such as `library()` run at the R prompt. Reading a page runs no analysis.

## Keep the work organised

Inputs belong in `data/`; generated tables and figures in `results/`;
learner writing in ignored `reports/`. Settings belong in `config/`.
Reruns replace named outputs, so copy an output folder before comparing
alternative settings. Do not reuse an incomplete run.

If an error occurs, record the exact command, message, R version and package
versions. Ask AI to explain that evidence, then check the proposed remedy.
